questions.q: Why can't the VM from Lesson 9 reach the storage account from Lesson 10 right away, and why is that correct?
options: Storage was locked to deny-by-default with public access blocked; that's the correct intermediate state until a scoped identity-based grant is made
It's a bug caused by a misconfigured subnet that needs to be fixed
The VM was deployed in the wrong region
Managed identities are not supported on VMs at all
questions.explain: Lesson 10 deliberately locked storage down; nothing can reach it until this lesson's scoped grant connects the two on purpose.

questions.q: What does az vm identity assign do?
options: Gives the VM a system-assigned managed identity, with no password or key generated or stored anywhere
Creates a new storage account for the VM
Generates a long-lived access key for the VM
Opens a network rule allowing the VM's subnet through the storage firewall
questions.explain: A managed identity is an Azure-managed identity for the VM itself, requiring no credential to be created, stored, or rotated.

questions.q: Why is the role assignment in this lesson scoped with --scope to the specific storage account rather than the resource group or subscription?
options: To grant only the exact permission actually needed on one resource, not broader access than necessary
Because Azure RBAC roles cannot be scoped to a resource group
Because the resource group does not support role assignments
Scoping has no effect on what the role can access
questions.explain: Scoping to the one storage account follows the least-privilege principle this program has taught since the identity chapters.

questions.q: What AWS mechanism mirrors the Azure managed identity pattern for an EC2 instance reaching S3?
options: An IAM role with a trust policy, wrapped in an instance profile, issuing temporary credentials via STS
A hardcoded access key stored in the instance's startup script
A public bucket policy allowing any authenticated AWS user
A shared account password distributed to the application team
questions.explain: The instance profile pattern is the identical mechanism the IAM fundamentals chapter already covered for this exact use case.

questions.q: Compared to an embedded credential, what's the real result of wiring compute to storage through a managed identity or IAM role?
options: No embedded credential exists anywhere in the chain for anyone to leak, commit to source control, or forget to rotate
The application runs slightly faster because no authentication occurs
The storage account no longer needs a firewall or access policy
The VM gains permanent, unscoped access to all storage accounts in the subscription
questions.explain: The entire point of this lesson's approach is eliminating the hardcoded-secret risk by removing the credential from the chain entirely.
